title: The Ascent to the Heavenly Jerusalem
english: The height of it: for thus it is possible to worship in spirit and truth 'the Lord King Pantocrator'.

Regarding the revealed understanding, the feast of the booths must be understood otherwise. Our human bodies are thus presented. Immediately indeed the most holy Peter, a disciple of Christ, writes: 'The Lord Jesus Christ revealed to me that the removal of my dwelling is near' (2 Cor 5:1). In agreement also the lawgiver Paul says: 'We who are in the tent groan, being weighed down, because we do not wish to be stripped off but to be clothed, so that the mortal might be swallowed up by life' (2 Cor 5:4).

Moreover the feast of the booths is fulfilled previously and especially by those promising 'rejoicing', not by men alone with women not having been defiled, but also by women hastening to have holiness in spirit and body.
In addition to these, those entering the honorable marriage also adorn their own booths, being pure and guarding their bed undefiled.

Furthermore, the festival of the booths is fulfilled even more highly, being crowned and made glorious in the expected time of the resurrection, of the corruptible body being raised incorruptible and of the psychic spiritual body being raised. Does not the body become a divine booth, sown in weakness and dishonor, so that it might rise in power and glory?

It is worthy to learn how this spiritual feast is celebrated on the fifteenth of the seventh month. For the celebrant must, through the interpreted booths, surpass the cosmos made in six days, resting from all service of worship, sabbath-keeping according to the 'Sabbath having been given to the people of God', which Jesus alone confirms saying: 'I will give you all who come rest' (Matt 11:28), and again: 'You will find rest for your souls' (Matt 11:29).

On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, those celebrating are 'those who have given a portion to the seven and also to the eight', adhering to the old and the new covenant; for through the seven the old is signified because of sabbath-keeping, but through the eight is the resurrection of Christ after the cross, having occurred on the eighth day, the Lord's day. [Zechariah 14:17: And it shall be that whoever does not ascend from all the tribes of the earth into Jerusalem to worship...].
To the King Lord Pantokrator, and these things shall be added to those.

Since the spiritual Jerusalem lies on high according to the philosophy of the writing Apostle, where it says: 'But the Jerusalem above', and where it says: 'You have ascended to Zion, the mountain and city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem', only those are ascending upon it who are able to say: 'But our citizenship is in the heavens' (Phil 3:20), and again: 'He raised us up' (Eph 2:6), God clearly, 'and seated us in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus' (Eph 2:6), while those of the tribes of the earth who are still 'bearing the image of the swine' (Ps 50:16) and 'thinking of earthly things' (Col 3:2) exist and are not ascending to see the beautiful city lying on high in peace.
Those not ascending shall be added to those from among all the nations who did not ascend, being persuaded by the same things as them.

Those thinking of earthly things who are not ascending because they are being carried down by the weight of earthly works, those having hurried to ascend into the city having broken foundations, through the one laying the foundation, the 'artisan and builder of it, the Lord' (Matt 7:24), shall worship the King Lord the Pantokrator with the angels. For it has been written: 'All the angels of God shall worship him' (Ps 90:7).

A Lord existing as a King and Pantokrator is declared not the Father without the Son nor the Son without the Father. For one kingdom and lordship is the same, and the pantokratic power is the same of the Trinity. Therefore, if a desire enters into us to worship the Trinity as King Lord Pantokrator, let us not remain among the tribes of the earth, but having stored up the heart there in heaven, so that we might... being in Jerusalem, we might worship with all the rational creation, 'bowing every knee to the King of the heavens and earth and those under the earth, for the glory of God the Father, every tongue confessing that Jesus is Lord' (Rom 14:11).

If the tribe of Egypt does not ascend and does not come there, and upon this there shall be the fall, which the Lord will strike all the nations, as many as do not ascend to celebrate the feast of the tabernacles: this shall be the sin of Egypt and the sin of all the nations, as many as do not ascend to celebrate the feast of the tabernacles (Zech 14:18).
That which has been lifted up in Jerusalem...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Reining of the Tongue
english: Regarding the celebration of the feast of tabernacles, its power and excellence have been stated previously, from which it is made clear what magnitude it is to ascend into the lying festival and what kind of fall those who have lagged behind this super-greatness experience.

Not only Egyptians, but all other nations will be struck down and fall by the economy of God, so that, having perceived that they are evil, they may take up a longing to 'establish a feast among those who crowd together,' which is the feast of tabernacles. There are two understandings of this feast, which have already been stated; it is necessary to diligently execute the advancements according to virtue 'with a voice of rejoicing and salvation' through divine love, so that, having ascended through these into the house which the Savior of all has founded for the ages of ages, we may praise Him who has brought [us] to Himself after many advancements, each to say faithfully and scientifically: 'Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place of the tabernacle of your glory.' For thus it is possible to say in the manner of hymnody: 'I encircled myself in his tabernacle and offered a sacrifice of shouting.'

He who attains this holy guidance of blessedness, even if he be Egyptian or from another nation, will cease [to be such], as before the fall, becoming a Jerusalemite according to the inner man, composed of fullness and perfect virtue.

And the holy word says that not to ascend to the appointed feast of tabernacles is a great sin. In the words of those who have perished, the spiritual tabernacling has been assigned in various ways, and every Egyptian and nation is to ascend upon it, as has been stated previously. For he will truly become an Israelite without guile, being a Jew in secret according to the inner man (Zach. 14:20–21: On that day the thing on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord God Almighty, and the bowls that are in the house of the Lord shall be like the pitchers before the altar, and every bowl in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holy to the Lord God Almighty).

On the day interpreted as the holy tabernacling, into which it is fitting to ascend and to celebrate, it is proper to worship the King Lord God Almighty; that which is on the bridle of the horse shall be called holy.

To the Lord Almighty. What is this other than the ongoing word forbidding the wildness of the entrails and the lack of virtue, which the wise man protects against those being preyed upon: 'Do not become like a horse or a mule, who lack understanding, being driven by bits and bridles of their jaws that do not draw near to you.'

How is the lustful horse, being preyed upon by shameful passions, not led by the spiritual rider, so that by restraining the unrestrained bearing of the beast, it might become useful for the day of battle, as it is proverbially said: 'A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but the help is from the Lord' (Proverbs 21:31).

Along with this horse-like manner, the untrained one, being allegorically a mule, is tamed, with bits and bridles of their jaws being drawn toward the best riders, so that yielding to the guidance of the bit, they may carry the rider in an orderly fashion.

This agrees with what is said from the Psalm, as the blessed James wrote in his epistle, regarding the holding of the restless tongue that has become wild through much talk that it ought not to say (James 3:6). His wording has it thus: 'We put the bit in the mouths of the horses, and we lead their whole body' (Psalm 32:9), so that there may be a straight course and a steady walk.
How much more it is fitting to rein in the tongue, that is, the word, so that it does not rush into a pit but remains harmless, as if the bit itself were dedicated to the Lord Almighty.

When the bit of the horse is sanctified, the cauldrons in the house of the Lord, in which the meat of the sacrifices is placed before the altar, shall be like bowls in which libations are priestically performed; just as having a cauldron and a bowl involves the same energy according to different thoughts, so too a libation and a sacrifice.

For just as in sensible things there is one libation and another sacrifice, and the cauldron and the bowl, so also in the intelligible things there is... differing in energy and thought. Immediately also, the Savior, being a true high priest and a lamb and a shepherd...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Canaanite as Allegory of the Unfaithful
english: He is addressed as such, because regarding sensible things it is not possible for the lamb of the one presenting him to God to be both high priest and to be called a shepherd of the same. For the high priest is to the altar and the shepherd is to the sheep. And if this is so, then the basin, allegorically, is the same as the bowl.

Concerning the spiritual bowls, in the Song of Songs the divine bride says concerning her brother: 'My sister has come down into his garden to shepherd the bowls of fragrance in gardens and to gather lilies' (Song of Songs 4:12). Some [ask] whether the bowls of fragrance into which the brother has descended are the divinely inspired writings, or rather their divine thoughts, in which the one who descended shepherds in gardens and gathers lilies bearing a spiritual fragrance of lilies being presented.

When the basins become bowls of fragrance before the face of the spiritual altar, then in this way every basin shall be holy in holy Jerusalem and in Judah. In this, Jerusalem is to be understood as the glorious Church, and Judah as he whom his brothers praise and whom the sons of his father worship. Who this is, is said in those things previously read from the prophet.

'And all those who sacrifice shall come and take from them and eat from them. And there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord of the Universe on that day' (Zechariah 14:21). All those performing the sacrifice of righteousness and the sacrifice of praise shall come to the one being worshiped and whom they serve, in order to glorify him, who exhorts them to this. For he says: 'A sacrifice of praise shall glorify me' (Psalm 50:23).

And they shall come to themselves with a harmonious disposition in order to perform at once the things of the priesthood, taking from the basins placed around the altar... lying so as to eat meat from the sacrifices in them, as has already been said. And since the function of the things of the destined basins is performed with word and scientific theory, it is appropriate that they are called bowls. For this form signifies a word, in the Song of Songs it is proclaimed...

It is said. For the bride makes known the beauty and the loveliness which she loved as a sister in her own soul: 'His sideburns, growing fragrant like the vessels of ointment' (Song of Solomon 4:2). The sideburn is a sign of the word of the source: even as the source dies, it flows and grows fragrant.

This mystical, intellectual worship being performed by those arriving to perform the spiritual liturgy, having cast the meats taken by analogy—namely those from calves and rams—into the holy vessels, a Canaanite shall no longer be in the house of the Lord Almighty on the day when the restoration of those [who were...] has occurred. For a Canaanite is the stranger from the womb as one being outside of piety; and he shall not be, either by changing into Israel, 'the true one not having deceit,' or by being cast out of the house of the Lord Almighty. A Canaanite is to be accepted allegorically even if he has fallen out of the Israelite state. Such was the other, according to Sossannus, a man staying as an elder, to whom the most wise Daniel says: 'Seed of Canaan and not Judah, your beauty has deceived you, and desire has turned your heart; thus you did to the daughters of Israel, and there they fear to consort with you, but a daughter of Judah did not endure your lawlessness' (Daniel 9:7). Hosea also agrees regarding the lawless ones, as if they were Canaanites having such a condition: 'Ephraim has set himself a stumbling block as a companion of idols. He desired Canaanites; by committing fornication, he has become a fornicator' (Hosea 4:17).

And since the lawless one is, according to tropology, a Canaanite, he is cast out of the holy house of the Lord Almighty, so that he may no longer be in it. The divine apostle Paul fulfills this in his letter to the Corinthian Church: 'For it is heard among you that there is fornication, and such fornication, which even is not among the Gentiles, that a man has the wife of his father. And you are such, and should not rather have mourned, so that the one who has done this thing might be removed from among you' (1 Corinthians 5:1, 5). And he has been cast out of the assembly of the faithful, so that, having perceived himself to be such an evil, he might come by his own intention to receive the penalty of his error, which indeed has happened, so as to be driven into...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
